# Final Audit — Project446 v0.7.6.8 Patcher

## Executive Summary

The patcher's structural coverage of csgo_gc.dll is complete and independently corroborated. Every one of the 20 unique `AddFinding` callers, every Win32 anti-cheat API caller (`OpenProcess`, `TerminateProcess`, `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`, `Process32*`, `VirtualQuery`, `SuspendThread`, `GetThreadContext`, `IsDebuggerPresent`, `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent`), and every `[AntiTamper]` log-string owner falls inside the 30-function patch table. The HWID assembler chain at `sub_101D3890` (MachineGuid + SMBIOS + WinDir volume serial + CPUID) is genuinely unreachable after the `HwidBuilder` (`sub_101D3C30`) JMP-to-cave; no MAC / HDD / WMI / adapter enumeration surface exists in this version. The auto-update fetch/apply chain (`sub_100B0050` / `sub_100B1270` / `sub_100B2EB0`) is patched at all three entry-points, and the Ed25519 verify / bundle stage routines are fully downstream of that patched chain.

Three real defects surfaced under skeptic review. First, a **residual restart-loop** at `sub_100859E0` (RVA `0x000859E0`) is tick-driven by `sub_10085F00` every frame, latches `byte_106F7E25=1` once a newer version marker appears in `csgo_gc/update_target.txt`, and then issues the engine `_restart` command as soon as the server drains — a single stale/planted `update_target.txt` produces an **indefinite reboot condition**, not the "nuisance" the source finding implied. Second, `HwidBuilder` (`sub_101D3C30`) has a **second caller** at `sub_100567A0` (MasterScan / AntiTamper) that feeds the assembled HWID string into `sub_1004D400` (AddFinding); this path is only neutralized because a different patched RVA happens to RET, an implicit coupling not surfaced in the design. Third, the 18-19 detector RETs share the identical 3-byte prologue `{31 C0 C3}` — trivially detectable by any whole-module hash comparison (Project446 backend cross-checking msg-9205 findings is the realistic threat model), and on `stdcall`/`fastcall` entry-points with stack args a bare `ret` risks caller-side stack imbalance.

Behavioral fingerprints dominate the residual risk surface. The Challenge9205 handler (`sub_1006F850`) hardcodes `result_code = 3` unconditionally into proto field 9, and — with `AddFinding` / `ScanEntry` / `MasterScan` patched to RET0 — the outgoing `CMsgGCCStrike15_v2_ClientReportValidation` carries an infinite zero-findings streak. Server-side entropy tracking on `result_code` distribution, unsolicited-vs-solicited 9205 ratio (currently exactly 0 because `MonitorLoop` and `NativeModFlush` are RETs), and pattern-analysis of persistent-clean replies are the one attack surface no in-DLL patch can close. Combined with the identical hardcoded `cpu=GenuineIntel-000906EA` string and the literal `0.0.0.0` `GetPublicIP` sentinel, every patched client emits a machine-clean profile that clusters trivially on the backend.

## Confirmed Gaps (prioritized)

### P0 — Restart-loop persistence via `update_target.txt`
- **RVA**: `sub_100859E0` @ `0x000859E0`, driven by `sub_10085F00` @ `0x00085F00`, drainage-gate `sub_1007D5F0`, dispatch `sub_1007C4D0`.
- **Mechanism**: reads `csgo_gc/update_target.txt` via `sub_100AFDF0` → `sub_100AFC70`, compares to embedded `"0.7.6.8"`, latches sticky flag `byte_106F7E25`, then on every tick issues `getenv("GC_UPDATE_RESTART_CMD")` (default `_restart`) once the server empties.
- **Impact**: indefinite reboot storm each session if a newer-version marker is planted or left on disk. Cannot overwrite the DLL (bundle apply is dead) but is user-hostile and denial-of-service-shaped.
- **Fix**: RET0 `sub_100859E0` at RVA `0x000859E0` (`31 C0 C3` is unsafe here because caller may pass stack args; use `33 C0 C2 04 00` or a proper stdcall-aware stub after confirming the calling convention). Do **not** stub `sub_100AFC70` — it is shared with the (allegedly patched) `sub_100B0050` write path.

### P1 — Whole-module hash detectability of 18 identical `{31 C0 C3}` RETs
- **RVAs** (spot-check): `0x00050D40`, `0x000567A0`, `0x00056E00`, `0x0004DDA0`, plus 15 `Det:*` entries in `g_patches[]`. The patch-list count itself is **off-by-one in the coverage narrative (4+15 = 19, not 18)** — reconcile.
- **Mechanism**: Project446 backend cross-checks msg-9205 replies against expected native findings; VAC does not ship `csgo_gc.dll`, but the Project446 server has every incentive to hash it. Naive signature-scanning for `{31 C0 C3}` will not detect (the pattern is too common); whole-section SHA/MD5 will.
- **Fix**: Vary prologues per detector — rotate through `{33 C0 C3}` (xor eax,eax alt), `{29 C0 C3}` (sub eax,eax), `{B0 00 C3}` (mov al,0), `{C2 00 00}` (stdcall clean-ret), or short-jump-to-cave with per-detector unique epilogue. Regenerate randomly per patcher build.

### P1 — `stdcall`/`fastcall` stack-cleanup risk in bare `ret` stubs
- **Evidence**: `sub_10056E00` (thin wrapper) and `sub_100567A0` show `and esp, 0FFFFFFF8h` alignment prologues and `arg_0/arg_4/arg_8` at `ebp+0x3C..0x44` — classic MSVC callee-cleans-stack layout.
- **Impact**: `{31 C0 C3}` (`ret` with no imm) leaves stack args on caller's stack. If any surviving caller was using stdcall convention, the caller's stack pointer walks off. `sub_10056E00` is a wrapper that tail-calls `sub_100567A0` — patching both is redundant; patching either wrong risks a crash.
- **Fix**: audit each detector's calling convention; use `ret imm` (`C2 XX XX`) where callee cleans, or `31 C0 C3` only where cdecl.

### P2 — HWID second-caller coupling not surfaced
- **RVA**: `sub_100567A0` @ `0x000567A0` calls `sub_101D3C30` (HwidBuilder) at `0x10056C21`, then feeds the HWID string to `sub_1004D400` (AddFinding) at `0x10056C33`. The spoofing analysis only enumerated the AUTH-frame caller (`sub_100D93B0`).
- **Impact**: currently benign because AddFinding is RET, but the "spoof at HwidBuilder is a single-choke-point" mental model is wrong — a second exfil channel exists via the AntiTamper report path. Future patcher revisions that spare `sub_1004D400` re-open it.
- **Fix**: also stub `sub_101D3890` (RVA `0x001D3890`) prologue with immediate empty-string return; and preemptively stub `sub_101D3430` (RVA `0x001D3430`) with `31 C0 C3`. Cheap defense-in-depth.

### P2 — Server-side behavioral fingerprints (msg 9205)
- **Hardcoded `result_code = 3`** (`sub_1006F850`, `v34 = 3` unconditional, mask `0x200` = proto field 9). Perfect entropy = 0 across every audit.
- **Zero unsolicited 9205 flushes**: `sub_10070150` (30 s tick) and `sub_1006FDF0` (native-silent flush) both patched to RET. **These are two independent threads** spawned from `sub_1006FC70` via `sub_10075B30` and `sub_10075AD0` — coverage confirmed both are patched; do not conflate as a single kill.
- **Zero findings streak** on challenge-solicited 9205: a real CS2 GS statistically emits benign findings (module rebases, overlay hooks). Infinite clean = anomalous.
- **Fix option A** (recommended): inject 1-2 plausible low-severity findings into the outgoing proto (module load event, page-guard flip) to break the entropy signature.
- **Fix option B**: MITM `gc.project446.su` WS and rewrite the payload; requires DNS/hosts control.
- **Fix option C** (weak): passive-capture real (unmodified) client traffic to `gc.project446.su`, diff `result_code` distribution, choose a matching hardcoded value or randomize over the observed set.

### P2 — Steam callback surface unpatched (real SteamID64 continues to flow)
- **Evidence**: `SteamAPI_GetHSteamUser` IAT (RVA `0x00546440`) is rewritten to `mov eax, <random>; nop`, but `SteamAPI_Init`, `SteamAPI_RegisterCallback`, `SteamAPI_RunCallbacks` are **not stubbed**. Genuine `steamID64` continues to arrive via Steam callbacks. Also, the fake `HSteamUser` is `random & 0x7FFFFFFF | 1` — same value across both call sites in one patcher run, so two patched clients from the same build collide.
- **Fix**: NOP the `SteamAPI_RegisterCallback` IAT site that installs GC-message callbacks in csgo_gc, or hook the callback dispatch to strip `steam_id` fields before they reach report queues. Regenerate fake handle per call-site.

### P3 — `GenuineIntel-000906EA` and `0.0.0.0` sentinels
- Every patched client emits identical `cpu=GenuineIntel-000906EA` (Skylake i7-6700K signature) inside the cave HWID string and identical `0.0.0.0` from `GetPublicIP` (`sub_100A1070`).
- **Fix**: randomize CPU signature per-machine (persist in `p446_hwid.txt`); randomize public IP to a plausible non-RFC1918 value per session.

### P3 — Dead-code WinTrust / CryptCAT wrappers not preemptively neutered
- **RVAs**: `sub_100515B0` @ `0x000515B0` (WinVerifyTrust), `sub_10051690` @ `0x00051690` (CryptCATAdminCalcHashFromFileHandle), `sub_10051800` @ `0x00051800` (dispatcher).
- **Correction to source finding**: `sub_10051800` uses short-circuit `||`, not `&&` — so only one primitive needs to return `true` to defeat the dispatcher. Patching both is belt-and-braces, not required.
